name: Database Connection Timeout
description: The application failed to communicate with the primary or inventory database cluster within the allotted time, usually due to high load or network failure.
patterns: FATAL: Connection to inventory-db-cluster failed after <NUM>ms
instructions:
Step 1: Check the database health metrics in your monitoring tool (e.g., Datadog, Grafana).
Step 2: Verify if there is a sudden spike in traffic causing query queuing.
Step 3: If the database is completely unresponsive, initiate a manual failover to the read-replica.

name: Missing Configuration Key
description: A required environment variable or configuration key was not found during the application's startup sequence.
instructions:
Step 1: Check the deployment logs to see which environment was being deployed (e.g., production, staging).
Step 2: Log into your Secret Manager (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault) and verify the key exists.
Step 3: Restart the application daemon to force it to pull the latest configuration.

name: Worker Out of Memory (OOM)
description: A background worker or cron job exceeded its allocated memory limits and was killed by the operating system.
patterns: FATAL: Heap out of memory in process <NUM>
instructions:
Step 1: Identify which cron job or worker was running at the time of the crash.
Step 2: Temporarily increase the memory allocation for that specific worker node.
Step 3: Create a ticket for the backend team to optimize the data parser to use streams instead of loading entire files into RAM.

name: Redis Cache Connection Refused
description: The application cannot establish a TCP connection to the Redis caching layer.
patterns: WARN: Failed to connect to Redis cache on port <NUM>
ConnectionError: Unable to reach Redis cluster
instructions:
Step 1: Verify that the Redis pod/instance is currently in a 'Running' state.
Step 2: Check the network security groups to ensure traffic is allowed on port 6379.
Step 3: If Redis is stuck in a bad state, flush the cache and restart the service.
